sections.content: You know *carro* from A1 Unit 8, *jugo* and *mesero* from A1 Unit 12 and *apartamento* from A2 Unit 16. These are Latin American words. Spanish has one grammar but many local words: the same thing can have a different name in each country, and learning to recognise them makes travel easy. Everyone understands the common ones, so use the word you hear around you.

sections.title: One thing, several names
rows: car (*carro*: Mexico, Colombia, Central America; *auto*: Argentina, Chile, Uruguay)
flat, apartment (*departamento*: Mexico, Argentina, Chile; *apartamento*: Colombia, Venezuela)
avocado (*palta*: Peru, Chile, Argentina; *aguacate*: Mexico, Colombia)
el colectivo / la micro / el camión / la guagua

items.spanish: Mi auto está cerca de la oficina.
items.english: My car is near the office.
My mobile phone does not work.

items.spanish: Vivo en un departamento pequeño en el centro.
items.english: I live in a small flat in the centre.

sections.content: Watch for the same word with different meanings. *Guagua* is a bus in Cuba and Puerto Rico, but a baby in Chile, Peru, Ecuador and Bolivia.
